      Abstract

      This submission formalises a depth hierarchy theorem for matrix-symmetric algebraic circuits, together with the characterisation of bounded-depth matrix-symmetric circuits by homomorphism polynomials on which it rests. A circuit with variables xi,jx_{i,j}xi,j​ for i,j∈[n]i, j \in [n]i,j∈[n] is matrix-symmetric if every permutation of rows and columns extends to an automorphism of the circuit. Its orbit size is the maximum size of an orbit of gates under these automorphisms, its support size is the least kkk such that every gate is fixed by the pointwise stabiliser of some set of at most kkk rows and columns, and its support depth is the maximum number of wires along a path at which the minimal support of a gate is not contained in that of its parent.

      Depth hierarchy. For Δ≥1\Delta \geq 1Δ≥1, let TΔ,nT_{\Delta,n}TΔ,n​ be the full nnn-ary tree of depth Δ\DeltaΔ, viewed as a bipartite pattern. Over a field of characteristic zero, for n≥20n \geq 20n≥20, every reduced matrix-symmetric circuit of support depth at most Δ\DeltaΔ computing the homomorphism polynomial hom⁡TΔ,n,n\hom_{T_{\Delta,n},n}homTΔ,n​,n​ has orbit size at least nlog⁡2n−Δlog⁡2log⁡2n−3n^{\log_2 n - \Delta \log_2 \log_2 n - 3}nlog2​n−Δlog2​log2​n−3, whereas for n≥5n \geq 5n≥5 it is computed by a reduced matrix-symmetric circuit of support depth at most Δ+1\Delta + 1Δ+1 and orbit size at most n2n^2n2.

      Characterisation. The patterns are measured by their Δ\DeltaΔ-forestwidth fwΔ(F)\mathrm{fw}_\Delta(F)fwΔ​(F), the least width of a tree decomposition of FFF of depth at most Δ\DeltaΔ with an empty root bag, a variant of the Δ\DeltaΔ-treewidth of Bhargav, Chen, Curticapean, and Dwivedi. For Δ≥1\Delta \geq 1Δ≥1, k≥2k \geq 2k≥2, and n≥2k+1n \geq 2k+1n≥2k+1, a polynomial ppp in the n×nn \times nn×n matrix variables is computed by a reduced matrix-symmetric circuit of support size at most kkk and support depth at most Δ\DeltaΔ if, and only if, ppp is a linear combination of homomorphism polynomials hom⁡F,n\hom_{F,n}homF,n​ of bipartite multigraphs FFF with fwΔ(F)≤k−1\mathrm{fw}_\Delta(F) \leq k-1fwΔ​(F)≤k−1. One direction is an explicit circuit construction for a single pattern, which additionally bounds orbit size, depth, and size; the other extracts homomorphism polynomials from a circuit by induction on its gates. Reduced matrix-symmetric circuits are shown to be rigid, and every matrix-symmetric circuit is shown to admit a reduced one computing the same polynomial without increasing size, depth, or orbit size.

      Further ingredients. The lower bound combines the characterisation with two further results, both proved here. The first is a support theorem: for n≥20n \geq 20n≥20 and 3κ≤n+23\kappa \leq n + 23κ≤n+2, a reduced matrix-symmetric circuit of orbit size less than (nκ)\binom{n}{\kappa}(κn​) has support size at most κ−1\kappa - 1κ−1. It is derived from a self-contained proof, for n≥20n \geq 20n≥20, of the theorem of Dixon and Mortimer that a subgroup of Symn\mathrm{Sym}_nSymn​ of small index contains the pointwise stabiliser of a small set in the alternating group, via Bochert's bound on bases of groups without 3-cycles, an analysis of orbits and block systems, and the simplicity of the alternating group. The second is a non-uniform homomorphism distinguishing closure result: if a graph class F\mathcal{F}F contains K1K_1K1​ and is closed under minors and under Roberson's weak oddomorphisms, G∉FG \notin \mathcal{F}G∈/F is connected, and GGG is a minor of the underlying graph of FFF, then hom⁡F,N\hom_{F,N}homF,N​ is not in the linear span of the homomorphism polynomials of patterns in F\mathcal{F}F for every NNN at least the size of a CFI graph of GGG. Its proof uses CFI graphs, a contraction formula for homomorphism counts, and a lifting of minor models.
